questions.q: When you `GROUP BY vendor_id, invoice_month`, what determines whether two rows belong to the same group?
options: Only vendor_id needs to match
Both vendor_id AND invoice_month must match — it's the combination that defines a group
Only invoice_month needs to match
Rows are never grouped together if there are two GROUP BY columns
questions.explain: With multiple GROUP BY columns, Oracle creates one group per distinct combination of all listed columns.

questions.q: Why is it safe to include `s.vendor_name` un-aggregated in SELECT when GROUP BY includes it and the query has joined on vendor_id?
options: It isn't safe — this would always cause an error
Oracle ignores vendor_name entirely in this case
Because vendor_name is listed in GROUP BY, and every row within a group shares the same vendor_name since they share the same vendor_id
vendor_name is automatically treated as an aggregate function
questions.explain: Since vendor_name is functionally tied to vendor_id (one name per supplier) and is included in GROUP BY, it never varies within a group.

questions.q: What does `TO_CHAR(invoice_date, 'YYYY-MM')` commonly get used for in a GROUP BY query?
options: Converting a number into a date
Removing NULL values from invoice_date
Sorting rows in descending order
Bucketing dates into a monthly grouping value for aggregation
questions.explain: Formatting a date down to year-month creates a text value that groups all dates in the same month together.

questions.q: In the Receivables mirror query, which table supplies the outstanding balance figure being summed?
options: AR_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL, via AMOUNT_DUE_REMAINING
HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS
RA_CUSTOMER_TRX_ALL
AR_CASH_RECEIPTS_ALL
questions.explain: AR_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL.AMOUNT_DUE_REMAINING tracks what's still outstanding on a transaction, mirroring AP_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL.AMOUNT_REMAINING.

questions.q: Why would supplier 101's January total and supplier 101's February total appear as two separate rows when grouping by both vendor_id and invoice_month?
options: Because Oracle always splits results by month regardless of GROUP BY
Because vendor_id cannot repeat across multiple rows
Because they represent two different combinations of (vendor_id, invoice_month), even though vendor_id is the same in both
This would actually produce an error
questions.explain: Multi-column GROUP BY groups by the combination of values, so the same vendor_id in two different months forms two distinct groups.
